I've thought through this season as your assigned farmer identity. Here is my management plan, saved to `farmer_plan_noedu_female_12mu.json`:

---

I am 43 years old and I've been farming this land for 20 years. I never went to school, so I don't read books about farming — I learn by watching and doing. My husband works construction in town and my daughter is in middle school, so mostly it's me and my mother-in-law handling the 12 mu. We grow wheat and then maize, same as everyone in the village. For wheat, I put down compound fertilizer at planting because the soil is tired after the corn, and I always topdress with urea at jointing. My neighbor Auntie Wang skipped the topdress two years ago and her wheat was so thin she cried at harvest. I irrigate three times for wheat — green-up, jointing, and grain filling — because wheat is our main food and income, and the well water is there. For maize, the time between wheat harvest and planting is so short, sometimes only two days if it rains, so I put all the fertilizer in at once and plant fast. I irrigate maize twice if the summer is dry, but usually the rains help. I hire two days of labor for each crop — one for planting and one for harvest — because my mother-in-law's back is not good and I can't do everything alone. It costs about 100 yuan per day now. I figure my total costs this year are around 5,500 yuan. That's a lot of money for us, but my husband sends some home from his construction job, and I would rather put enough fertilizer than risk a bad year. I remember 2019 when we had a dry spring and the corn that got less fertilizer barely made any ears. I don't want that again.
